result:
The implementation is complete and matches upstream Jinja's actual fix. Summary of changes:

**`src/jinja2/parser.py`**
- `parse_primary` gained a `with_namespace` param: when set and a `name` token is followed by a `dot`, it parses an `NSRef` (`ns.attr`) instead of a plain `Name`.
- `parse_tuple` gained the same `with_namespace` param, threading it into the primary-parse closure used for `simplified` (assignment-target) tuples.
- `parse_assign_target` no longer special-cases namespace refs before tuple parsing; it now just forwards `with_namespace` into `parse_tuple`/`parse_primary`, so `ns.attr` can appear anywhere inside a tuple target like `{% set x, ns.a, y = 1, 2, 3 %}`.

**`src/jinja2/compiler.py`**
- The "is this a `Namespace` object" runtime check moved out of `visit_NSRef` (which could previously emit a statement mid-expression when the ref was inside a tuple) and into `visit_Assign`, which now walks `node.find_all(nodes.NSRef)`, dedupes by name, and emits each check as its own statement before the assignment line.

Also added three regression tests in `tests/test_core_tags.py` (namespace-only tuple swap, mixed name/namespace tuple, and the invalid-namespace-in-tuple runtime error) and a `CHANGES.rst` entry. Full suite: 909 passed.
